MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 20, 2025
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS AND TELECONFERENCED
  6:30 P.M.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meating to order at 6:33 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons wero recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Skylar Peak, and Commissioners Drew Leonard,
  John G. Mazza, and Elizabeth Riddick

  ALSO PRESENT: Joseph Toney, Acting City Manager; Kellan Martz, Assistant City
  Attorney; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Tyler Eaton, Principal Planner; Patricia
  Salazar, Development and Operations Manager; Courtney Brown, Associate Planner;
  Alexander da Silva, Assistant Planner; Larbi Azzaz, Assistant Planner, Parker Davis,
  Media Technician; Gail Duncan, Administrative Assistant and Rebecca Evans, Recording
  Secretary

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge ofAllegiance was led by Dennis R. Smith.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

CONSENSUS Commissioner Mazza moved and Chair Hill seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda as recommended by staff.

  The motion carried unanimously by consensus.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on February l7, 2025.

  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 25-37 and
  consider an Ordinance to amend the Malibu Local Coastal Program and Zoning

  rebuilding of structures damaged or destroyed by natural disasters, including but

  provide relief for those affected and provide a recommendation to the City Council
  regarding the amendments.

  Acting City Manager Toney introduced Principal Planner Eatont

  The staffreport was presented by Principal Planner Eaton.

  Disclosures:  Chair Hill

CONSENSUS The Commission limited public comment to two minutes per person and suspended
  donations oftime for in-person speakers due to the number of speakers present.

  Chair Hill opened the public comment portion ofthe hearing.

  Speakers: Abe Roy, Don Schmitz, Norm Hainey. Wade Majors, Jo Drummond,
  Colin Drummond, Lester Tobias. Doug Burdge, Thomas Torres, Sion Roy, Arnold
  Bernstein, Arno Koch, Carl Randall, Luis Tena, Scott and Naomi Richter, Paul
  Grisanti, Georgia Goldfarb, Mike Moore, Richard Gibbs, Megan Lorick, Luca
  locovoni, Chris Deleau, Amy Ablakat

RECESS  At 8:02 p.m. Chair Hill recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:07 p.m.
  with all Commissioners present.

  Speakers: A. K. Munaim, Jed August, Robert MacLeod, Jimmy Petulla, Patty
  Phillips, Nora Cohen, Janet Fulk, Kaden Andrews, Sam Marshall, Andrew Sheldon,
  Ronmi Zoriu, Brian Merrick, Carmel McFayden, Dean Leonard, Bethany Mayor,
  Daphne, Geoffrey von Oeyen, Michael Kureth

  Heather Naylor and Gigi Goyette did not respond when called for public comment.

  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Hill closed the public comment
  portion ofthe public hearing and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Commission directed questions to staff.

  At 9:01 p.m. Assistant City Attorney Martz issued a first warning to a member of
  the public and at 9:02 p.m. Chair Hill called for removal ofa person who was not
  following the rules of decorum for the proceedings.

RECESS  Chair Hill recessed the meeting at 9:04 p.m. to restore order. The meeting resumed
  at 9:12 p.m. with all Commissioners present.

  The Commission resumed deliberations and directed questions to staff.

RECESS  At l l :45 p.m. Chair Hill recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at l 1:50 with
  all Commissioners present.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved and Commissioner Leonard seconded a motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 25-37, as amended. l) adding recital G, to
  state, “February l3, 2025, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-20-25,
  which suspended requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act and
  California Coastal Act for Palisades Fire rebuilds and related issues”; 2) modifying
  Local Implementation Plan (LIP) Section l3.4.6(A)(2) to change “floor area,
  height or bulk” to “footprint and height’“ 3) modifying LIP Section 13 4 l l(A)(4)
  to meet the minimum FEMA flood zone requirements even it nonconfoxming,

  4) modifying LIP
  Section 13 4 ll(A)(5) to delete  O  , 5)

  movmg the De Minimis Waivers from LIP Section 13.4.1 l(A) to LIP Section
  13.4.6 — Exemption for Structures Destroyed by Natural Disaster; 6) recommending
  City Council consider removal ofthe current ingress/egress requirements in Malibu
  Municipal Code (MMC) Section 17.44.090 based on consultation with a fire expeit;
  7) adding ficus to the list of trees prohibited within 50 feet ofa structure to Malibu
  Municipal Code Section 17.53.090(C)(1)(c); 8) recommend a fire expert review
  Malibu Municipal Code Section 17.53.090 prior to staff presentation to City
  Council; 9) striking staff‘s recommended addition of MMC Section
  17.60.020(C)(l); 10) recommending City Council meet with external agencies
  including California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) and California
  Coastal Commission to discuss those agencies’ viewpoints on construction of a
  seawall and protection of Pacific Coast Highway infrastructure; 1 l) recommending

  facing blufftop” with “coastal bluff”; 15) adding to MMC Section
  17.40.040(A)(k), “Temporary housing supported on wheels shall be fastened to the
  ground”; and l6) recommending approval of an Ordinance to amend the Malibu
  Local Coastal Program and Zoning Text Amendment to amend Title 17 of the
  Malibu Municipal Code to facilitate the rebuilding of structures damaged or
  destroyed by natural disasters, including but not limited to, the 2025 Palisades Fire,
  2024 Franklin Fire, and 2024 Broad Fire to provide relief for those affected.

  The Commission discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

CONSENSUSAt 12:17 p.m. the meeting was adjourned by consensus in memory of the fire
  Victims.
